source.ref: https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go/pull/1354; AACR-Bench dataset.json rows 140, 141, forbid seeds rows 1605-1609; hand-checked 2026-10-23 by vetter A; the pull request's next commit, d83519214f (Fix spaces), fixed row-140 before merge

rationale: The change removes System.NewLine and rewrites output calls to fmt.Fprintln and literal newlines. row-140 is kept as required: at head both watch-mode status lines pass a literal ending in a space to Fprintln, which adds its own separator, so the output gains a doubled space; it is in the diff, no linter reports it, and the author fixed it in the pull request's next commit (author-fix). AACR-Bench marks the comment as a person's, but on GitHub it was posted by the Copilot reviewer, so the producer names it; its stated detail (a space before the newline) was also wrong and is corrected here. row-141 is dropped: line 83 of watcher.go is a commented-out call, so it has no runtime consequence. The five forbid seeds (rows 1605-1609, written by a model) say the literal newlines bypass sys.NewLine or break CRLF handling; that method no longer exists, the pull request description states that output now uses a line feed on every platform on purpose, fmtMain is unreachable, and the blank-line check compares against the same literal every line is built with. Three of them become forbid ranges: the formatter settings, the trailing blank-line check and the help header and examples.

expect.concern: Fprintln always inserts a space between operands, so the literals that already end in a space make watch mode print a doubled space before the build start time and before the build duration.

forbid.reason: fmtMain is unreachable (its only caller is commented out) and the pull request deliberately uses a line feed everywhere, as the language service already does; a hardcoded LF here is not a regression.
Every line the help generator builds now ends in the same literal line feed, so the trailing blank-line check cannot mis-detect anything on CRLF systems.
Help output uses a line feed on every platform on purpose, as the pull request description states; System.NewLine no longer exists, so there is no abstraction being bypassed.
